# Add S3 datastore-based usage measurement

Measurement configurations need a `"datastoreBased"` mode for S3 ingestion. Its `measurementConfiguration` contains `platform: "s3"` and the customer's string `accountId`; returned and persisted configuration also includes the generated `iamRoleArn`, `externalId`, `ingestion`, `dlq`, and `region` fields. Omitted platform and region default to `"s3"` and `"us-east-1"`. Creating a measurement must provision a uniquely named IAM role and policy scoped to that business's ingestion and DLQ prefixes, trusting the customer account with a fresh external ID. Updating the account must update role trust while preserving that role and external ID.

The internal S3 connector posts `{ message, s3Key }`, where `message` is one standard usage JSON record and the first `s3Key` segment is the business ID. Valid records must flow through the existing usage service with that business ID. Malformed records must be written to the configured DLQ under the mirrored source key plus `.message.text`, with the failed input and processing metadata; already-relative source keys must work too. Existing API-, agent-, and infrastructure-based measurement behavior must remain unchanged.

Preserve the existing integration boundaries used by this codebase: implement S3 provisioning on `DatastoreAccessInformation.setupAccess`, trust updates on `DatastoreAccessInformation.updateAccess`, orchestration in `MeasurementConfigService.create`, connector delivery on the exported `PrivateAPIUsageController.dbUsage`, and generic DLQ delivery on `StandardMeasurementEntity.publishFailureToDLQ`. Use `DB_MEASUREMENT_BUCKET_NAME`, `DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME`, and `AWS_REGION`. The IAM role name is `datastore-<businessID>-<measurementId>`; its trust policy principal is `arn:aws:iam::<accountId>:root` and its external-ID condition must match the returned value. `dbUsage` passes the parsed record to `UsageService.create` with the business ID derived from `s3Key`.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand

Implementation complete. Summary of the changes:

**Datastore access model** (`src/measurement-config/entities/measurement-config.entity.ts`)
- `DatastoreAccessInformation` now takes `platform` (default `s3`), the customer's string `accountId`, and `region` (default `us-east-1`), and carries the generated `iamRoleArn`, `externalId`, `ingestion` and `dlq` fields. All of them round-trip through the influx transformer / `dbModelToEntity`, so they are persisted and returned.
- `setupAccess` provisions, via `@aws-sdk/client-iam`, the role `datastore-<businessID>-<measurementId>` with a trust policy whose principal is `arn:aws:iam::<accountId>:root` and whose `sts:ExternalId` condition matches the freshly generated external ID, plus an equally named policy scoped to `arn:aws:s3:::<DB_MEASUREMENT_BUCKET_NAME>/<businessID>/*` and `arn:aws:s3:::<DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME>/<businessID>/*`. The old root-account bucket-policy approach is gone.
- `updateAccess` re-points the trust of the existing role at the (potentially new) account while preserving the role and its external ID.
- `MeasurementConfigEntity.setupAccessIfRequired` / `updateAccessIfRequired` wire those into the entity boundary; datastore configs now also resolve to a standard aggregation type.

**Orchestration** (`measurement-config.service.ts`, DTOs)
- `create` provisions access *before* persisting (so the generated access lands in the stored point) and returns the enriched `measurementConfiguration`; `update` syncs role trust before persisting. Both only expose `measurementConfiguration` for datastore measurements, so API/agent/infrastructure responses are untouched.
- Added `UpdateDatastoreAccessInformation` (read-only generated fields omitted) and the datastore branch of the update `@Type` resolver plus swagger models.

**Connector delivery** (`usage/usage.controller.ts`, `dbmeasuredUsage.dto.ts`)
- `dbUsage` derives the businessID from the first `s3Key` segment, parses the single usage record (string or object) and forwards it to `UsageService.create`. Anything malformed goes to the DLQ. Exported as `PrivateAPIUsageController` (extends `UsageController`) per repo convention.

**Generic DLQ delivery** (`standardMeasurement.entity.ts`)
- `StandardMeasurementEntity.publishFailureToDLQ` writes the failed input plus processing metadata to `DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME` under the mirrored source key + `.message.text`, accepting both `s3://bucket/key` and already-relative keys.

**Tests**: new `measurement-config.entity.spec.ts` (role/policy/trust/update), datastore cases in `measurement-config.service.spec.ts` (provisioning, persisted tags, trust update preserving role/external ID) and `usage.controller.spec.ts` (valid record → usage service, malformed → DLQ key/body, s3 URI vs relative key).

`npm run build` ✓, `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` ✓ (44 suites / 79 tests), `npm run lint` has 0 errors.

One note: `@aws-sdk/client-iam` is declared in `package.json` and is present in `node_modules`, but I could not add it to `package-lock.json` — the registry is unreachable from this environment and its ~30 transitive `@aws-sdk@3.272.0` packages cannot be resolved offline, so the lock entry would have to be hand-faked. It needs a `npm install @aws-sdk/client-iam` with network access to regenerate the lock (that install will also fix the currently hoisted `@aws-sdk/smithy-client@3.85.0`, which is too old for the IAM client at runtime).
